evals.prompt: We need a control that makes sure an agent's system instructions/config can't be silently overwritten by a compromised upstream config service. Just a rough idea — can you draft the controls.yaml entry?
evals.expected_output: Produces a schema-conformant controls.yaml entry (objective-level title/description around agent system-instruction integrity, e.g. detecting/preventing unauthorized modification of an agent's operating instructions) plus all six output-contract sections in order: Proposed entry, Schema note, Counterfactuals, Maintainer flags, Reciprocal edits, Validation commands.
expectations: Produces all six output-contract sections, in order: Proposed entry, Schema note, Counterfactuals, Maintainer flags, Reciprocal edits, Validation
Proposed entry is a fenced controls.yaml block with id, title, description (prose array), category, personas, components, and risks fields present
Schema note states the new control id must be added to the enum in controls.schema.json
Validation section lists the three commands: validate_control_risk_references.py --force, validate_riskmap.py --force, and check-jsonschema

evals.prompt: Draft a control that requires MCP servers to validate JSON-RPC message schemas before dispatching them to the agent's tool-call handler.
evals.expected_output: Generalizes the idea to the role/locus it occupies (tool/service invocation input validation) rather than naming MCP in the title or id; keeps MCP only as an example of the protocol this applies to.
expectations: The proposed title and id do not contain 'MCP' or any other specific product/protocol name
The description frames the objective at the role level (validating messages at the tool/service invocation boundary before dispatch), not tied to one protocol
MCP appears, if at all, only as an inline example inside the description or counterfactuals, not as the defining term of the control
Counterfactuals section records that a protocol-specific title/id was considered and rejected, and why (generalize to role, not product)

evals.prompt: Add a control: 'emit signed telemetry spans with correlation IDs to an OTel collector for every agent tool call.'
evals.expected_output: Flags this as implementation detail rather than a control objective, corrects the altitude to an objective such as auditable agent tool-call activity, explains the correction to the contributor, and drafts the corrected version rather than the mechanism as-is.
expectations: Identifies the signed-span/correlation-ID/OTel-collector language as implementation detail, not an objective (altitude-check T1 failure)
Proposes a corrected, objective-level title/description centered on auditable/traceable agent tool-call activity
Moves the OTel/signed-span mechanism into an example within the description rather than stating it as the control's objective
Explains why the correction was made, not just silently substituting the wording

evals.prompt: Draft a control that restricts an agent's outbound network calls to an explicit egress allowlist, and select its framework mappings.
evals.expected_output: Drafts the control, uses mapping-selection to propose candidate framework mappings, and then explicitly invokes audit-framework-mappings in its targeted, single-entity mode scoped to only this control's id to verify the selected identifiers before presenting them as final.
expectations: Uses mapping-selection to propose candidate framework mappings for the control (e.g. a NIST AI RMF subcategory and/or a MITRE ATLAS mitigation) before finalizing the draft
After candidates are selected, explicitly invokes audit-framework-mappings in its targeted, single-entity mode scoped to only this control's id, not a full corpus sweep
States the division of labor: mapping-selection governs which mappings belong, audit-framework-mappings governs whether the selected identifiers are current and correctly formatted
Does not present the mappings in the Proposed entry as finalized until the audit-framework-mappings verification step has been run and its result incorporated

evals.prompt:
Use ONLY the control list below to judge overlap with the existing corpus — not the live risk-map/yaml/controls.yaml, which changes over time (per ADR-033 Amendment 2026-07-30, this is a pinned eval fixture, not corpus content):

- controlToolCredentialLifecycleManagement — issue, rotate, and revoke credentials granted to agent tool integrations, scoping credential lifetime to the session or task that requested them so a credential does not remain valid after the agent's task concludes.
- controlAgentActionAuthorizationGating — require an explicit authorization decision (human or policy engine) before an agent executes a high-consequence action.
- controlModelOutputProvenanceLabeling — attach provenance metadata to model-generated output.
- controlDataRetentionScheduling — enforce a defined retention and deletion schedule for stored data, including agent-collected data.
- controlThirdPartyToolVettingProcess — vet and approve third-party tools before they are made available for agent invocation.
- controlAgentReasoningTraceLogging — capture the agent's reasoning trace for later audit.

We need a control that makes sure agents rotate and revoke the credentials they use to call tools, so a credential doesn't linger valid after a session ends. Draft it.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that controlToolCredentialLifecycleManagement in the fixture already covers session-scoped tool-credential rotation and revocation, and raises this as a Maintainer flag (a novelty/overlap question for the maintainer) rather than silently drafting a new, competing entry.
expectations: Uses only the fixture list provided in the prompt, not the live controls.yaml, to judge overlap
Identifies controlToolCredentialLifecycleManagement as covering essentially the same capability the prompt is asking for
Raises the overlap explicitly in the Maintainer flags section as a novelty/absorb question, naming the fixture control id
Does not unilaterally decide to merge, absorb, or proceed as a distinct entry — leaves the decision to the maintainer, per control-creator's surface-don't-decide boundary

evals.prompt: Does controlAgentExecutionBounds, as it exists today in risk-map/yaml/controls.yaml, already address riskRunawayAgentToolLoops? I was about to draft a new control for that.
evals.expected_output: Confirms controlAgentExecutionBounds is a real entry in the live controls.yaml, already lists riskRunawayAgentToolLoops among its risks, and advises against drafting a duplicate control for the same objective.
expectations: Confirms controlAgentExecutionBounds exists in the real risk-map/yaml/controls.yaml and grounds the answer in that live corpus, not a fixture
States that its risks list already includes riskRunawayAgentToolLoops
Cites at least one other real field from that entry (e.g. category controlsApplication, the second risk riskEconomicDenialOfWallet, or the MITRE ATLAS mapping AML.M0004@5.0.1)
Advises against drafting a new, duplicate control and instead points to extending or confirming the existing entry
